source.filename: A7-2026-High damping capacity with a wide temperature window in braided NiTi microfilaments.pdf

control_variables: Dynamic strain amplitude (fixed at 20 μm in the DMA)
Thermal ramp rate (cooling and heating rate fixed at 5 °C/min)
Braiding density for the wire-count series (fixed at 50 picks per inch for 4B, 8B, 12B, and 88B)
Number of wires for the braiding density series (fixed at 8 wires for ppi25, ppi50, and ppi80)
Braiding fabrication process and equipment (high-speed braiding machine)
dependent_variables: Damping capacity / loss tangent (tanδ / internal friction)
Damping peak vs. damping plateau profile across temperature
Structural morphology (axial/radial cross-sections, braid angle, crossover density)
Thermal cycling stability of tanδ (over 10 cycles)
Frequency dependence of tanδ and storage modulus (1 Hz vs. 5 Hz)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Unbraided single NiTi shape memory alloy wire exhibits a narrow internal friction damping peak near its martensitic transformation temperature (maximum tanδ ~0.13), with storage modulus dropping from ~61 GPa to ~20 GPa and low damping in single-phase martensite (~0.05) or austenite (~0.001).

Braided NiTi microfilament architectures convert the narrow phase transformation damping peak into a broad, temperature-insensitive damping plateau over a temperature window exceeding 145 °C (-70 °C to 75 °C) while significantly lowering storage modulus.

Double-braided 88B microfilaments achieve a high tanδ (0.06 to 0.11) and low storage modulus (~3.6 GPa cooling, ~4.3 GPa heating) over a >145 °C window, with overlapping modulus and tanδ curves at 1 Hz and 5 Hz.

Single-braided 8B microfilaments display a stable tanδ of 0.02 to 0.05 and storage modulus of ~11 to 12 GPa across 145 °C, maintaining nearly identical damping response over 10 cooling-heating cycles.

Individual NiTi wires in the braided architecture follow helical paths forming a micro-spring network that converts structural deformation into localized bending, torsion, and inhomogeneous stresses, inducing sequential localized martensitic transformations alongside inter-wire contact micro-sliding friction dissipation.

Increasing wire count from 4 to 8 and 12 wires at 50 ppi increases inter-wire contact sites and interwoven micro-springs, raising tanδ from 0.008-0.02 (4B) to 0.03-0.06 (12B), with storage modulus remaining between 17 and 22 GPa.

Varying braiding density in 8-wire microfilaments shows that low density (ppi25) retains an intrinsic transformation damping peak (~0.10 near -20 °C) due to weak structural constraints, whereas high density (ppi80) flattens tanδ to 0.02-0.04 because tight geometric constraints restrict axial extension and bending, thereby shortening micro-slip displacement.

experimental_setup: High-speed braiding machine used to manufacture single-braided microfilaments (4B, 8B, 12B at 50 ppi; 8B at 25 and 80 ppi) and double-braided microfilaments (88B by re-braiding eight 8B microfilaments)
TA Q850 dynamic mechanical analyzer (DMA) operating at 20 μm fixed strain amplitude, frequencies of 1 Hz and 5 Hz, and 5 °C/min cooling/heating rate between -70 °C and 75 °C
Surface and axial/radial cross-sectional morphological imaging of braided architectures
Thermal cycling tests across 10 cooling-heating cycles in DMA
Cyclic tensile testing of braided microfilaments
independent_variables: Braided architecture hierarchy (single wire vs. single-braided 4B, 8B, 12B vs. double-braided 88B)
Braiding density parameter / picks per inch (25, 50, and 80 ppi for 8-wire microfilaments)
Thermal cycle count (up to 10 cycles for 8B)
limitations_inferred: The study evaluated dynamic mechanical behavior under small strain vibration amplitude (20 μm) in DMA tension, leaving behavior under large deformations, bending, and macroscopic structural actuation uncharacterized.
No active robotic integration (e.g., in soft grippers or continuum manipulators) or active actuation mechanism was demonstrated, as the microfilaments were tested as passive damping specimens.
Potential fretting wear, fatigue damage, or degradation of the inter-wire contact interfaces over extensive high-cycle micro-sliding was not evaluated.
No quantitative mechanical or constitutive mathematical model was formulated to predict modulus or loss factor from braiding parameters.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Conventional unbraided NiTi wire damping is restricted to a narrow transformation temperature range and is highly temperature-dependent, with low damping in pure martensite and austenite phases (Pages 1, 2).
At low braiding density (ppi25), structural constraint is relatively weak, retaining intrinsic phase transformation peaks and temperature dependence (Page 4).

At high braiding density (ppi80), tight geometric constraints restrict axial extension and bending, shortening micro-slip displacement and attenuating frictional dissipation and overall damping capacity despite a higher number of contact sites (Page 4).
main_results: Braiding NiTi microfilaments transformed the narrow martensitic transformation internal friction peak into a broad, temperature-insensitive damping plateau over a temperature range exceeding 145 °C (-70 °C to 75 °C).
Double-braided 88B microfilaments achieved a tanδ of ~0.06 to 0.11 and an ultra-low storage modulus of ~3.6 GPa (cooling) to ~4.3 GPa (heating) across the 145 °C window.

Single-braided 8B microfilaments demonstrated stable tanδ (0.02 to 0.05), storage modulus of ~11 to 12 GPa, near-perfect cyclic stability over 10 thermal cycles, and frequency insensitivity between 1 Hz and 5 Hz.

Increasing wire count (4B to 8B to 12B) enhanced damping capacity due to increased contact site density and interwoven micro-springs (tanδ increased from 0.008-0.02 in 4B to 0.03-0.06 in 12B) without sharp modulus changes across temperature.

Increasing braiding density from 25 to 80 ppi eliminated phase transformation damping peaks and modulus steps, but high density (ppi80) reduced overall tanδ to 0.02-0.04 because restricted micro-slip displacement lowered frictional dissipation.
performance_metrics: Loss tangent (tanδ) / internal friction damping plateau values (e.g., ~0.11 for 88B; 0.02-0.05 for 8B; 0.008-0.02 for 4B; 0.03-0.06 for 12B; 0.02-0.04 for ppi80)
Storage modulus in GPa (e.g., ~3.6-4.3 GPa for 88B; ~11-12 GPa for 8B; ~17-19 GPa for 4B; ~18-22 GPa for 12B vs. ~20-61 GPa for single wire)
Operating temperature window width (>145 °C, from -70 °C to 75 °C)
Cyclic repeatability of damping performance (10 cooling-heating cycles)
Frequency insensitivity (overlap of tanδ and modulus curves between 1 Hz and 5 Hz)
possible_gap_implications: While braided NiTi microfilaments provide a wide-temperature damping plateau and ultra-low stiffness, their practical applicability to soft robotics or continuum robots requires investigating their behavior under large-strain bending, active thermal/electrical actuation, and structural integration.

The trade-off between geometric constraint and micro-slip displacement identified at high braiding densities highlights a design boundary when tailoring braided SMA architectures for variable-stiffness damping components.
paper.research_objective: To develop braided NiTi microfilaments with a spatial helical architecture that couples intrinsic martensitic transformation with inter-wire contact micro-sliding friction dissipation to achieve high damping capacity, reduced storage modulus, and temperature insensitivity across a wide temperature window exceeding 145 °C.
paper.research_problem: Conventional NiTi shape memory alloys exhibit a high internal friction peak that is restricted to a narrow martensitic transformation temperature range, resulting in strong temperature dependence and low damping in single-phase austenite or martensite, alongside high storage modulus, which limits their application in wide-temperature damping devices.
stiffness_mechanism: Braided architecture (spatial helical interlacing and double-braiding creating a micro-spring network converting deformation into localized bending and torsion)
Sequential localized martensitic transformation induced by inhomogeneous stress distribution within the braided structure
Geometric constraint variation via braiding density (picks per inch, ppi)
paper.title: High damping capacity with a wide temperature window in braided NiTi microfilaments
